title: KML Placemark Counter: Feature Census
description: Count the Placemark elements in a KML file with the KML Placemark Counter — feature-level size checked locally before import. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a real-estate KML with 214 Placemarks is 214 listings wearing geometry — a number worth knowing before you promise anyone the file is 'small'.
quick_answer: The KML Placemark Counter counts the <Placemark> elements in a KML file — the features that usually carry a point, line or polygon plus its properties. Drop the file and read the feature count locally, before importing, comparing or sharing a file whose size you should know.

Last quarter's file: 1,204 placemarks. This quarter's: 1,187. Seventeen features vanished somewhere — the count starts the investigation the diff finishes.
Converting KML to another format is priced by features, not megabytes. This is the number quotes are built on.
The source database holds 860 sites; the KML holds 860 Placemarks, or the export dropped some — verify before the client counts for you.
One Placemark can hold a MultiGeometry of 30 polygons — feature count 1, coordinate blocks 30. Both censuses are printed on this site because maps break on geometry while databases break on features.
A Placemark may carry only a name, a description and a camera view — it still counts as a Placemark element. Structural counting is literal: the element is the unit.

faq: Does it count Placemarks inside Folders?
Yes — nesting is organisation, not a different element. Every <Placemark> in the document counts, at any depth.
No — overlays are their own elements, not Placemarks. The census is strict about the element it names.
Why is my count lower than the rows in my GIS?
Empty-geometry rows sometimes export as nothing, and some exporters split multi-part features. The count shows the file's truth; reconcile against the source with the named counter's audit.
Multi-part exports can duplicate features, and template Placemarks hide in some files. The viewer shows what the count found.
Does a Placemark need geometry to count?
No — the element counts as written. Geometry-free Placemarks are legal KML and occasionally intentional (views, labels-in-waiting).
Bytes follow coordinate tuples and description HTML more than feature count. Both numbers together size a file honestly.
Because a converted file can be recounted, and equal counts are the cheapest proof the conversion lost no features.
